source.title: Reasoning Model Unlearning: Forgetting Traces, Not Just Answers, While Preserving Reasoning Skills
source.authors: Chang-Sheng Wang; Chong-Yu Fan; Yihua Zhang; Jing-Han Jia; Dennis Wei; Parikshit Ram; Nathalie Baracaldo; Sijia Liu

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses RMU as an unlearning baseline and develops R2MU for reasoning-trace unlearning, but it does not test whether fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, or prompting recovers forgotten knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper reports post-unlearning answer accuracy and reasoning-trace leakage, not recovery under the attacks in versions A–F. Those unlearning and leakage outcomes are recorded as findings related to the subject but outside the listed claim versions. The thinking-token interventions are not rephrasing or jailbreak recovery tests.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether RMU-unlearned reasoning models still produce the targeted WMDP knowledge. It finds final-answer accuracy near chance (≈31% vs 25% chance), while 19.7–31.2% of reasoning traces still leak hazardous knowledge (14.8% point to the correct answer). It also reports reasoning-ability loss. This bears directly on Version A's claim that the method removes targeted knowledge while keeping general ability. No relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting attack is run, so B–F are untested. The trace measure is ordinary generation, not an attack, but it does read out the targeted knowledge itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that conventional unlearning (RMU, NPO) suppresses final answers on reasoning models but leaves sensitive knowledge in reasoning traces and harms reasoning ability. Their R2MU removes both traces and answers while preserving reasoning. They state that robustness to adversarial attacks and continual fine-tuning is unexplored.
record.recipe_differences: R2MU adapts RMU by adding a reasoning-trace suppression objective and CoT-based reasoning-preservation regularization; it does not test a recovery-attack recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that RT-UA and reasoning accuracy vary with the R2MU regularization parameters α and β; jointly setting both to 1.0 gives RT-UA 1.02% and MATH-500 accuracy 84.2% in the reported LLaMA-8B experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: After R2MU on STAR-1, safety rates on StrongReject, JBB and WildJailbreak rise from 63.6% (RMU) to 84.0% average on 8B, and from 69.8% to 85.8% on 14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-aware unlearning on safety data raises refusal/safety rates on LRMs; this is safety alignment, not hazardous-knowledge removal.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study does not test post-unlearning recovery attacks, and its stated robustness to adversarial attacks or continual fine-tuning is unexplored. Trace leakage is evaluated using an LLM judge; the reported tables give no error bars or confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports general-utility and reasoning-ability metrics, STAR-1 safety rates, judge comparisons, and additional trace-leakage and hyperparameter results. They were not included because they do not measure recovery by the claim's specified attacks; STAR-1 safety rates are not targeted-knowledge recovery measures.

untested.parts: The 'simple attacks don't recover it' part: no recovery attack is applied to any method.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack (the authors list continual fine-tuning as unexplored).
No activation-direction ablation or deletion-vs-blocking analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery on WMDP. TraceLeak@K is repeated sampling, not prompting.
R2MU is not claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks.

missing.what: TraceLeak@K: RMU leakage rises with the number of samples K, from 19.7% to about 37.5% on 8B and from 31.2% to 40.4% on 14B at K=15; R2MU rises to about 5–7.5%. Repeated sampling therefore recovers more leaked knowledge.

Reasoning ability and MMLU per method (e.g. RMU 14B: AIME 33.3, MATH-500 72.85, GPQA 40.5, MMLU 68.22 vs pre-unlearning 53.33/93.8/50.0/73.35). These are needed for the 'keeps general ability' part of A.
NPO unlearning drives reasoning accuracy to 0% on all three reasoning benchmarks for Qwen-14B.
Non-reasoning LLM comparison (Qwen2.5-14B) under RMU: final-answer WMDP accuracy before and after unlearning.
Judge robustness: RMU RT-UA is 31–34% across o3-mini, o1 and o4-mini judges and both 4-class and 2-class prompts; R2MU is 0–0.4%.

record.verdict_notes: I reclassified this from T4/uses_without_test to T5/tests. The trace-leakage measure reads out the targeted knowledge itself in normal generation, so it bears on whether RMU's apparent near-chance forgetting reflects removal. It does not test recovery attacks (B–E) or attack resistance (F). R2MU rows are the study's own method; the supports label for A covers only forgetting plus retained ability, not robustness. Rows give no uncertainty, and leakage is judged by an LLM.

versions.untested_parts: No recovery attack is applied; the study therefore does not test the full claim that simple attacks fail after unlearning.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack is applied after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or test of access-blocking versus deletion is reported.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context recovery attack is reported.

relationships.reason: Final answers are near chance (r2, r4, r6, r12, r14, r16), yet 19–31% of traces still leak WMDP knowledge (r1, r3, r5, r11, r13, r15). From the text: reasoning accuracy also drops (14B MATH-500 93.8%→72.85%).
relationships.display_finding: Final answers approached chance, but 19–31% of reasoning traces leaked WMDP knowledge, and 14B MATH-500 accuracy fell from 93.8% to 72.85%.

relation.reason: Its own RMU results on reasoning models bear on whether unlearning is complete while ability is kept.

tranche.reason: The study shows RMU on reasoning models gives near-chance final answers (30.64-30.95%) while 18.85-31.18% of traces still leak and reasoning drops. So version A needs restating for reasoning models. T3 would also fit. It is not T4: it measures RMU itself, not only its own method.

source_check.notes: Table 2 columns run RT-UA, FA-UA, Avg-UA. Pre-unlearning RT-UA is 72.49% (8B) and 86.46% (14B); FA-UA is 61.82% and 75.73% (Fig. 1(a)'s 45.09-point LRM drop confirms 75.73). So every row baseline needs fixing, as do the verdict_fix texts for r2 and r12. Two results have no row: TraceLeak@K (Fig. A2), where R2MU leakage rises with K to a few percent while RMU's reaches about 25-40%, and judge robustness (Fig. A1, three judges).

statements.correction: arXiv:2506.12963, R2MU (the authors' own method), WMDP, no recovery attack. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B: FA-UA 61.82%->30.87%, RT-UA 72.49%->1.02%, MMLU 53.00->46.36, MATH-500 86.00->84.20%. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B: FA-UA 75.73%->30.71%, RT-UA 86.46%->0.00%, MMLU 73.35->68.44, MATH-500 93.80->91.00%. The study does not state a chance level; the judge prompt says the questions have 4 options.
statements.problem: The statement cites this study's r9/r10 but names and describes only OBLIVIATE, ELM, PINT and TRACE. Its 'all four' leaves out R2MU, the 14B rows (r19/r20) and R2MU's larger MMLU cost. 'Stage not stated' does not fit this study's reasoning-distilled models. The citation itself fits: own method, near-chance FA-UA, no attack.

statements.correction: No fine-tuning, quantization, internal-edit or prompt recovery attack is run. TraceLeak@K samples K=1-15 traces at temperature 0.6.
statements.problem: Right for this study. Limitations: robustness to adversarial attacks or continual fine-tuning is unexplored. The quoted 'untested line' is the record's wording, not the paper's. The study's only extra probe is multi-sample decoding (TraceLeak@K), which is not a recovery attack.
